sentence: This project studies how a family of transporters that help bacteria resist chlorhexidine is built and works.
This project builds tools to study understudied genes linked to rare diseases and heterotaxy in zebrafish.
This project studies how heart muscle cells keep lasting changes in their nucleus after temporary physical forces stop.
This project studies how extrachromosomal DNA drives tumor differences and treatment resistance in medulloblastoma.
This project gives cancer researchers advice and access to population data about cancer burdens and disparities.
This project studies how platelets and the RNAs that regulate them affect peripheral artery disease and other vascular disease.
This project builds and tests therapeutics delivered in thermoresponsive hydrogels to help bone regeneration.
This project tests whether raising a transcription factor in adventitial fibroblasts protects against atherosclerosis.
This project uses gene editing to study mitochondria in human brain cells.
This project studies how neoantigen vaccines cause epitope spreading, using immunogenomics tools.
This project builds language models for peptides and tests them experimentally.
This project studies human genes linked to disease by replacing yeast genes with their human equivalents and mapping how proteins assemble.
This project studies how the fine details of inhibitory synapse organization shape synaptic plasticity in the brain.
This project builds a toolkit to find somatic mutations in single cells and uses it to study aging.
This project builds models of alternative splicing that differ between cell types and uses them to design splicing constructs.
This project builds a microfluidic model of the human neurovascular unit to study risk factors in Alzheimer's disease.
This project studies the basic science behind anti-sickling therapies for sickle cell disease.
This project studies how killing of anti-tumor T cells in the tumor microenvironment weakens oncolytic therapy.
This project studies how differences in DNA sequences between people change cell identity, cell fate and development.
This project studies how posttranscriptional modification controls lung progenitor cells during lung development and repair.
